title: refactor: structure visible and enforced
desiredOutcome: The module structure is written in one place, generated into the guide, and breaks the build when violated: _deps.py holds the layer table and lints the real import graph (no cycles, no upward edges, no unassigned file, hooks import nothing from scripts); the guide's module map is generator output under a drift lint; every script has a tree entry and a section, enforced; every big file is navigable by headers, enforced; CONTRIBUTING carries the add-a-script checklist and the decision record (folders declined with a revisit trigger at 40+ files, usage_ledger split deferred with its trigger, typing ban rationale).

tasks.title: _deps.py: the layer table and the import-graph lint
tasks.description: New flat module in house style (safe_stdio, N/M selftest). LAYERS as data: L0 _output,_ui_theme,_loader,_fmt,_manifest_io / L1 _areas,_policy,usage_ledger / L2 _help / L3 _panel_settings,_panel_ui,_panel_discovery,_report_html,_report_ui / L4 _panel_state,_report_usage / L5 _panel_write / L6 the twelve entry points - derive the true edges from real imports first and adjust the table to reality, the inventory is the starting truth. AST-walk scripts/*.py flat (mirror _output's scanners): sibling import edges. Assert: acyclic; every edge points to a strictly lower layer; every .py is assigned a layer (a new file without one is a named red - the folder without folders); hooks/*.py carry no static import of any scripts module. Selftest: green on the real tree + named fixture cases (cycle, upward edge, unassigned file, hook importing scripts), each mutation-proven.

add: _deps: real tree acyclic + layered + fully assigned; fixture cases each named

outcome.technical: _deps.py: LAYERS as data (8 layers, 29 modules), import_graph over static sibling imports (83 edges), layer_violations (cycle, upward edge, unassigned/stale, hooks-imports-scripts) with named tuples, deterministic --render. The real graph corrected the sketch: _output is the sole floor (every __main__ imports safe_stdio) and _help sits above _panel_settings (the deliberate s8 local import). One genuine finding: hooks/_config.py:603 statically imports _manifest_io (guarded, with fallback) - carried as the exactly-one known exception the selftest asserts; recorded as F11 for its own fix. 18 cases, upward-edge check mutation-proven.
outcome.descriptive: The module structure is now data with a lint: a cycle, an upward import, an unplaced file or a new hooks-to-scripts dependency breaks the build by name - and its first run found a real one.

add: map drift: the guide's fenced block equals _deps --render output

tasks.title: guide completeness + enumeration lint
tasks.description: The guide's tree gains the 16 missing scripts files at the neighbors' granularity; section 2 gains short sections for the 20 scripts files without one (2-4 sentences, derived from each module's docstring, pointing at it rather than duplicating it) and meter-usage.py on the hooks side. The stale 'all fourteen' count at ~:477 stops asserting a number. Lint in _deps' selftest: every .py under scripts/ and hooks/ must appear in the tree AND have a section heading - a missing file is a named red. Existing headings untouched; the new sections are new headings, which the drift lints allow.

add: enumeration lint: every script/hook present in tree + sectioned, missing one named red

outcome.technical: 18 tree lines and 20 new ### sections (the lint found three beyond the sketch: _areas, _panel_ui, _report_ui were treed but sectionless); the stale 'all fourteen' asserts no number. _deps.guide_enumeration with the shared-heading rule stated in its docstring; 25 -> 30 cases; round-trip red proven by deleting the usage_ledger tree line and watching e1 name it.
outcome.descriptive: Every shipped Python file has a tree line and a section, and losing either fails the build by filename.

verifiedBy: round-trip red on deleted tree line

tasks.title: section headers everywhere + navigability lint
tasks.description: Comment-only diffs: house-style '# --- x ---' headers for the 5 files with none (_report_usage 1365, _areas, _output, _panel_ui, _report_ui) and meaningful non-selftest sections for the big selftest-only files (render-report 1611, _policy 726, validate-manifest 850, validate-config, gen-demo-*, migrate-manifest, _fmt, _report_html, _loader) and the six hooks without one. Then the lint in _deps' selftest: every .py over 400 lines carries at least 2 non-selftest section headers; threshold a named constant with its reason; mutation-proven.

add: navigability lint: >400-line file without 2 non-selftest headers is a named red

outcome.technical: House headers added to 22 files (comment-only, additions-only, counts unchanged), _deps.navigability_violations with _NAV_MIN_LINES=400 and its reason; the lint's first real-tree run found two violators outside the declared scope (_manifest_io, _panel_settings) which the plan gate correctly refused - scope was extended by the orchestrator, both files headered, and the temporary exception list retired to zero. _deps 30 -> 34 cases (exception cases replaced by a clean real-tree assertion); fixture + mutation proofs kept.
outcome.descriptive: Every big file is navigable and a bare one over 400 lines fails the build by name - with zero exceptions left standing.
